answer: A farm must hence either lie, which the nectar graph proves on replay, or recruit 92 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the wharf registry records each claim and the inlet audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 79% of the attester's bond. That is 10 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
